title: PR's branch deleted, the PR itself never closed
author: off-by-one
description: Compares the repository's own Activity feed against its own pull request set: a pull request's head branch was deleted upstream, but the PR itself was never closed. GitHub does not auto-close a PR just because its source branch disappeared -- it sits open, unmergeable, silently orphaned, unless a human notices by hand and closes it.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long ago the branch-deletion event fired while the PR still reads open, mirroring duplicate-issue-still-open's own 24h grace window: under 24 hours scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- a branch deleted minutes ago may just be an in-progress rebase, not yet a real gap), at or past 24 hours scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal: an exact ref match between a real deletion event and a PR's own head branch. A deleted branch with no matching open PR, or a PR whose branch was deleted after it already merged or closed some other way, is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden.
